messages.subject: Issues using corspec
messages.body_plain:
Hi all,

I am currently using the corspec function and have trouble with it, I
need help!
I have already written a script to prepare my soundfiles and do the
frequency spectra using meanspec. This involved cutting the sound
files to get the signal only and get rid of the silence on each side
of the signal, doing a band-pass filter to keep frequencies from 500
to 10000Hz only, and calculating the mean spectrum of 10 different
calls from one individual.
So there was some matrix modifications involved, and I saved the data
as a two-columns text file, using
write.table(specMean, "SpecM1_2m", row.names=FALSE)

Then I tried comparing two spectra using corspec, and got this error
message:
Erreur dans cor(x = spec1, y = c(spec2[(i + 1):n2], rep(0, i)), method
= method) :
  'y' must be numeric

I checked my specs, and found that the column names had been changed
in the process to "V1" and "V2" so I changed them back to "x" and "y",
but it still doesn't work.

My "spec" variable looks like this:
> head(spec1)
          x          y
1 0.5167969 0.03273822
2 0.5598633 0.09213714
3 0.6029297 0.09989777
4 0.6459961 0.07955930
5 0.6890625 0.08882194
6 0.7321289 0.08160801

Do you have an idea to get it work?

Also, I suggest that the option of choosing a F-min and F-max to band
pass the sound could be added directly to the corspec function. What
do you think?

Thank you for your help.

messages.body_plain:
Hi,

I would double check that the values in your matrices/data.frames are
numeric. Sometimes when you load in data files, the values are imported
as text rather than numbers.

To check:

 > class(spec1$x)

if you get "numeric", then there is a different problem. However, if you
get "character" then the problem is that R views your values as text.

To change it, you could run

 > spec1$x = as.numeric(spec1$x)
 > spec1$y = as.numeric(spec1$y)

(There is probably a more elegant way of doing this, but this is the
quick and dirty way).

Let me know if this helps!

Steffi

messages.body_plain:
Hi,

Here is the script below. I also copied the data file, but maybe you
would rather have me send it to you as a text file on your email
address?
The thing is, you can read it but I don't think you can actually run
it because you would need the sound files and the "coordcriMcd" file
that gives the begining and end times of the signals in the sound
files.

Tell me if you need anything more!
Thanks again

SCRIPT

## CREATION DES SPECTRES FREQUENTIELS MOYENS EN VUE DE LA CORRELATION
DE SPECTRES

library("seewave")
library("sound")
library("signal")

setwd("/Users/Solveig/PhD/PROPAG/PROPAG CD C1-C20/CD C1-C20 pour DFA/
Sel_C1-C20_2m")

bird = 1 # A CHANGER POUR CHAQUE OISEAU ET CHANGER AUSSI LE NOM DU
FICHIER A LA FIN
nbcalls=10

specTot<-matrix(data=NA, nr=221, nc=11) # création de la matrice vide
complète pour les 10 cris

# On charge les 10 cris de l'oiseau sélectionné
for(call in 1:nbcalls) # boucle pour chacun des cris de chaque
individu
{ # boucle for

	if(call==1)
	{ # boucle if
son<-paste((past<-(paste("Mcd",bird,sep="","call"))), call,
sep="",".wav")
son<-try(loadSample(son), silent=TRUE)

# on charge le fichier avec les données de début et de fin de chaque
cri
coordcri<-read.table("coordcriMcd.csv", header=TRUE, sep=";", dec=",")

debcri<-coordcri[10*(bird-1) + call,3]
fincri<-coordcri[10*(bird-1) + call,4]

spec<-meanspec(son, wl=1024, from=debcri, to=fincri, plot=FALSE) # F
spec moyen
specfilt<-matrix(data = NA, nr=221, nc=2)

# On fait une bande passante de 500 à 10000 Hz. Pour une wl=1024, cela
correspond aux rows 12 à 232.
	for(i in 12:232)
	{
		specfilt[i-11,]<-spec[i,]
	}

specTot[,1]<-specfilt[,1] # on charge les données de fréquence dans la
première colonne
specTot[,2]<-specfilt[,2] # on charge les données d'amplitude dans la
seconde colonne
	} # fin boucle if
	else
	{ # boucle else

son<-paste((past<-(paste("Mcd",bird,sep="","call"))), call,
sep="",".wav")
son<-try(loadSample(son), silent=TRUE)

# on charge le fichier avec les données de début et de fin de chaque
cri
coordcri<-read.table("coordcriMcd.csv", header=TRUE, sep=";", dec=",")

debcri<-coordcri[10*(bird-1) + call,3]
fincri<-coordcri[10*(bird-1) + call,4]

spec<-meanspec(son, wl=1024, from=debcri, to=fincri, plot=FALSE)
specfilt<-matrix(data = NA, nr=221, nc=2)

	for(i in 12:232)
	{
		specfilt[i-11,]<-spec[i,]
	}

specTot[,call+1]<-specfilt[,2] # on charge les valeurs d'amplitude
seules dans les colonnes suivantes (la première colonne donne les
valeurs de fréquence pour tout le monde, conditionnées par la wl de
1024).
	} # fin boucle else
} # fin boucle pour chacun des cris de chaque individu

specMean<-matrix(data=NA, nr=221, nc=2) # on créée la matrice vide
finale
specMean[,1]<-specTot[,1] # on met les valeurs de fréquence dans la
première colonne

specAmp<-matrix(data=NA, nr=221, nc=10) # on crée une nouvelle matrice
pour y mettre seulement les valeurs d'amplitude
for(j in 1:10)
	{
		specAmp[,j]<-specTot[,j+1]
	}

specMeanAmp<-rowMeans(specAmp, na.rm=FALSE) # on fait la moyenne des
amplitudes des 10 cris pour chaque row
specMeanAmpCol<-cbind(specMeanAmp) # on transforme le vecteur de ligne
à colonne
specMean[,2]<-specMeanAmpCol[,1] # on ajoute les valeurs de moyennes
d'amplitudes à la matrice finale de résultats

write.table(specMean, "SpecM1_2m", row.names=FALSE)

THEN

spec1<-read.table("SpecM1_2m", header=TRUE)
colnames(spec1)<-c("x","y")

Ok, so the reason why corspec didn't recognised my data was that I
saved it as a data.frame (using write.table). So we need to convert
the data to a matrix :

spec1 <- as.matrix(spec1)
spec2 <- as.matrix(spec2)

Then corspec works:
corspec(spec1,spec2)

Thank you Jerome!
